analyticalQuestion: Can a quantitative complex-time/Jensen cover pay the distinct positive-entry times left by R0.71P without a lower anchor, truncation tax, or cover tax?
takeaway: A fixed finite classical truncation admits an anchor-taxed Jensen bound, but exact analytic families separately force lower-anchor, component-union, and window-cover costs.

panels.A: Temam lobe, certified disk, and inverse strong-norm scale
panels.B: near-sharp Blaschke anchor tax and squared positive entries

claimBoundary: Panels B-D are analytic counterfamilies, not Navier-Stokes trajectories. Panel A uses a classical strong-solution complex-time theorem. No uniform NSE zero count, continuation, singularity, regularity, originality, or Millennium-problem claim is shown.
